approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from two accepted molecular centers. Each region generates bounded paths of graph mutations and connected-fragment crossovers, fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process to its own episode records, and competes for the announced evaluation batch through raw-score Thompson samples. The models share a response amplitude estimated from the accepted session archive, while their conditioning labels remain local. Accepted feedback updates the generating region; measured progress expands or contracts its path support and eventually restarts an unproductive episode. Crossover partners currently come only from up to eight nearby records owned by that episode.
approach.novelty: Make the other region’s current accepted center available as one additional crossover donor. Freeze both centers at the batch boundary, retain every original local donor, and apply the existing score order and quantile draw to the augmented menu. This opens a missing structural recombination input without borrowing its label into the receiving model. The coverage sibling changed which existing proposals were purchased; context siblings borrowed predictor labels; other siblings changed restart location or progress accounting. This intervention instead changes which already accepted graph can supply a fragment to the inherited crossover constructor.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting Parent behavior is structural donor isolation after successful local-model execution. In n-7d1e6230ecce, all 870 recorded regional donor menus omit the distinct current opposite center; 19 menus have no local donor at all. The actual local_donors implementation restricts eligibility to episode-owned records, excludes its own center, takes the nearest eight, then score-ranks them. Independent read-only reconstruction over all fifteen frozen Search cells confirms the frozen policy audit exactly. All cells completed with 4,350 paid optimizer observations; mean endpoint is 0.58461375649735, seed-macro population SD 0.01681763193120207, and full/late global gain masses are 5.641824681825611/0.8322070529143051 over 4,350/2,175 purchases. Shared amplitude improved its own Parent by 0.01323001671094833, but this Parent remains 0.022416559713781 below formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de. The coverage sibling n-1cd50f38b9c4 bought from every region at every boundary but lost 0.004773190607384977; variance-context n-ded8f57a69ad gained only 0.0005827761218230032 and global-progress n-970847a1987c gained about 0.001512, below their registered criteria. Their executed predictions do not test donor access. Source: nodes/n-7d1e6230ecce/optimize.py; nodes/n-7d1e6230ecce/analysis.json; nodes/n-1cd50f38b9c4/analysis.json; nodes/n-ded8f57a69ad/analysis.json; nodes/n-970847a1987c/analysis.json. Every per-seed summary/run log, per-cell audit and its underlying trajectory/log file is enumerated and hashed together in policy/scratch/r0055-02-improve-L01/evidence-manifest.json. Missing support is measured; improved donor utility remains the hypothesis.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the exact frozen r55-origin-support-and-sharing-review and its recorded queries; the query strings are inherited search provenance, not claimed new searches. Reopening the TuRBO primary PDF confirms independent local models with global sample allocation; its continuous trust-region mechanics are not added. The Jensen PMC reopening encountered a browser challenge, so its finding is reused from the frozen review rather than represented as newly read text. Existing source and receipts establish the implementation boundary: augment accepted graph donor support while preserving predictor membership, auction and controller. Neither paper establishes utility for this donor-sharing rule; the complete paid-conversion test supplies that answer.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The frozen policy review checks the separation of local predictive models from graph-generation inputs. The actual intervention follows Parent source and all fifteen admitted Search receipt streams: the opposite accepted center is absent in every donor menu, while completed coverage, predictor-context and progress changes do not meet their utility criteria. This adds no literature-derived operator, model, estimator, continuous trust box, geometric constraint or new asset. The single appended donor and unchanged ownership rule are the campaign hypothesis.

hypothesis: Modify only the support of the existing crossover-donor law. After inherited retirements/restarts have finished and before either regional fit/generation, snapshot both current accepted centers once for the announcement. For region r, construct exactly its original at-most-eight nearest episode-owned donors excluding its current center. Append frozen center c_(1-r) once if its canonical identity differs from c_r and is absent from that menu. Sort the resulting at-most-nine records by the inherited (-score, accepted serial) key, and use the unchanged quantile edges, weights, within-group random draw and per-action current-walk-source exclusion. Eligibility of the extra accepted graph permits the existing crossover branch, including at an otherwise donorless singleton, but does not force a crossover or purchase. The branch probability and fragment constructor remain inherited. New accepted products retain their generating region and episode ownership. The opposite label is used only by the pre-existing donor ordering and already-shared amplitude archive, never imported into the receiving GP or credited to its controller. The predicted path is admitted donor support -> actual opposite-center recombination -> valid noncopy paid products -> owned feedback and useful full/late conversion.

finding_summary.headline: Cross-region recombination reached purchases and local learning, but both global-gain rates fell and mean score lost 0.0281
finding_summary.insights:
Missing donor access was a real structural restriction, but removing it was not sufficient to buy more useful global progress. Direct and earlier-cross products supplied only 0.22972 of the total global gain. Their descendants were productive in some cases: 2,015 unique later purchases were linked through actual accepted roots or successful donors. That ancestry cannot be converted into incremental causal credit, because the donor-free alternatives and their future trajectories were never evaluated.

The measured bottleneck moves beyond simple access. Direct recombinants were overpredicted by 0.10293 score units on average, compared with 0.03075 for remaining purchases; their prediction MSE was higher in 13 of 15 cells. Late in search the 148 direct products were overpredicted by 0.17822 on average and generated only two strict global gains, totaling 0.00229. The 59 earlier-cross-only late purchases generated none. A ranking model that can calibrate recombinations outside local training support is therefore a relevant method class for this observed limitation, although these selected-stream errors do not establish that misranking caused the score loss or tell us which unpurchased alternatives were better.

The chemistry also limits what broader access means. The accepted output broadened from 1,880 to 2,038 typed scaffolds and from 1,234 to 1,300 generic scaffolds, so this is not whole-search scaffold collapse. Yet high-score cohorts still contain only 7–25 generic scaffolds per task, 2,113 of 2,175 late purchases make no strict global improvement, and many outputs elaborate recurring ring/carbonyl families into strained or reactive arrangements. Small fragments increased from 134 to 177 accepted outputs while oversized graphs fell from 245 to 153; peroxide-containing outputs increased from 48 to 237, and 2,705 products had potential tetrahedral centers with no assigned configuration. Those observations support a gap in proposal operators that preserve coherent, chemically explicit frameworks while changing them. They do not establish a chemistry filter, size threshold or score-mediated benefit. What this node settles is that this exact donor-support rule activates without satisfying its full-and-late utility criterion. Better structural proposals, calibrated pricing and the wider regional approach remain open; no retained component or entire route is rejected by this single intervention.
finding_summary.results:
The structural access and feedback links worked. Across all fifteen Search sessions, the other accepted center was added at 864 of 870 regional boundaries; at the remaining six it was already present. The original donor set, independent training ownership and auction rules were preserved. There were 19,430 opposite-center draws and 261 paid products with a witnessed final noncopy two-fragment join, appearing in every session. Another 116 purchases had a successful earlier cross-region recombination followed by edits. Of these 377 products, 346 entered a later owned fit; 25 arrived at the final boundary and six belonged to an episode retired before another fit. No eligible product missed feedback use.

That access failed the registered useful-conversion prediction. Total global improvement fell from 5.64182 to 5.22074 across 4,350 paid evaluations, so gain per purchase fell from 0.001297 to 0.001200. Late-half gain fell from 0.83221 to 0.63777 across 2,175 purchases, or 0.000383 to 0.000293 per purchase. Mean endpoint fell from 0.58461 to 0.55654, a loss of 0.02807 against the code Parent rather than the required gain of 0.002. All three seed means declined; seven task/seed cells improved and eight worsened. Four task means fell, with median_2 the exception. The result is also 0.05049 below the formal Anchor. Every task completed its budget, with no evaluator invalid or duplicate submission and no model fallback. The verdict refutes the frozen utility prediction while preserving the established activation and feedback results.

molecular.headline: Aromatic polycycles and amine/carbonyl frameworks coexist with reactive bonds, strained rings and unresolved stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-de8f05115faf produces connected, mostly neutral, ring-rich structures spanning recognizable aryl amides, aza-aromatics, cyclic amines, fused dicarbonyl heterocycles and much less conventional bridged or contracted graphs. The exact frozen context reports both a complete Child evaluation and complete pairing with code Parent n-7d1e6230ecce on Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectories were present and read; no task or paired trajectory is missing. Structural aggregates below exclude the ten initial records per session: each side has 4,350 accepted optimizer records, 870 per task. These are evaluated outputs, not every internally generated or rejected graph. Digest ring-closure rates are 0.9529-0.9632 and aromatic-text presence rates 0.8943-0.954; these are molecule-level text flags, not aromatic atom fractions. RDKit perception gives a Child median of 29 heavy atoms and four rings, with a 1-110 heavy-atom range. There are 2,038 distinct nonempty typed Murcko scaffolds and 1,300 generic ones across the Child, versus 1,880 and 1,234 in the Parent. This supports broad graph diversity, while the strongest observed cohorts remain concentrated in recurring local families. The chemical changes are mixed: N-halogen-containing outputs fall from 1,017 to 326, O-halogen outputs rise from 104 to 126, and O-O-containing outputs rise from 48 to 237. Outputs below six heavy atoms rise from 134 to 177, while those above fifty fall from 245 to 153. Potential tetrahedral stereocentres occur in 2,705 Child molecules versus 2,113 Parent molecules, with no assigned tetrahedral configurations on either side. Only one Child output carries a formal charge. Synthetic plausibility is a structural reading, not a route, geometry, stability or biological-utility assessment. Functional-group patterns and ring flags are precisely defined in policy/scratch/r0055-02-improve-L01/molecular/summary.json; potential stereo uses RDKit FindMolChiralCenters including unassigned centers. That file cites every run-relative input and its SHA256. policy/scratch/r0055-02-improve-L01/molecular/provenance.json preserves the exact original staging paths and hashes together with byte-identical Child snapshots. The Parent inputs remain its published Search trajectories. Per-task high and low cohorts mean the 87 highest and 87 lowest recorded scores among the 870 optimizer outputs, respectively; tied boundaries use trajectory order. No objective chemistry specification is inferred beyond these observed associations, and no chemistry association attributes a component effect.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly medium-sized fused aromatic/carbonyl structures: median 24 heavy atoms, three perceived rings and twelve aromatic atoms; the full range is 1-45 heavy atoms. The high cohort spans 22-26 heavy atoms. Seed 0 reaches benzocyclobutene-like aryl carbonyl hydrazone/imine chemistry; seed 1 favors aza-indole carboxamides bearing aldehyde and N-S functionality; seed 2 favors densely fused N-O-containing rings with ketone, aminomethyl and thiol substitutions. These retain recognizable medicinal-chemistry fragments, but their assembled connectivity is frequently more questionable than an ordinary stable aryl amide. Compared with the Parent, N-halogen outputs decrease from 414 to 27 and small fully aromatic perceived rings from 222 to nine; N-N and N-O bonds instead become common. Nonempty typed/generic scaffold counts are 285/150 versus 298/161.
liabilities: The leading benzocyclobutene-like structure carries an unsaturated four-membered fused ring, terminal imine and hydrazone functionality; the seed-1 leader carries an aldehyde and an N-S bond. These create stability and synthesis questions not resolved by their scores.
Thiol-bearing and N-O-bridged polycycles can be difficult to prepare and characterize; no stereochemical assignment or geometric feasibility evidence accompanies them.
Thirty-five accepted outputs have fewer than six heavy atoms, including molecules at zero score.
missing_features: Stable alternatives that retain the compact carbonyl/aromatic arrangement without terminal imines, N-N/N-S substitution or dense N-O ring fusion are poorly represented among the cited leaders; their score advantage is untested.

Nitrile-bearing alternative frameworks seen in the Parent high cohort are absent from the Child high cohort: zero versus 72 of 87. This is lost sampled coverage, not evidence that a nitrile is a required answer.
Specified stereochemical identities are absent despite potential tetrahedral centers in 292 outputs.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited seed-0 leader scores 0.4714045207910317 and has 24 heavy atoms, three rings and an aryl carbonyl framework. Seed-1 and seed-2 leaders both score 0.4597940970593737 despite differing connectivity. All 87 high-cohort outputs carry a carbonyl, versus 26 of the low cohort; the low cohort has median eight heavy atoms and includes the zero-scoring OS, F and acyclic polyene. Within the seed-2 family, the N-O cyclic structure scores 0.458386638264238, its thiol variant 0.4597940970593737, and the ring-edited C1NC analogue 0.21964598551080294. This supports retention of a compact carbonyl-bearing ring arrangement, not indiscriminate heteroatom addition. Parent per-seed best scores were 0.42762099872850584, 0.5423261445466404 and 0.4478476056206344; the chemistry differs by seed rather than showing one uniformly recovered motif.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most heavily decorated output family: median 40 heavy atoms, six perceived rings and 21 aromatic atoms, with a 1-104 heavy-atom range. Halogens occur in 0.892 of optimizer SMILES by the digest text flag. The seed-0 leader is a linked aza-aromatic/dicarbonyl system with nitrile and aldehyde groups; seed 1 reaches an extensively substituted dicarbonyl heterocycle attached to an O-O-O-containing ring; seed 2 converges on an anilino fused aza-dicarbonyl core with a crowded oxygen-bridged ring system and chloromethyl substituents. High-score graphs are generally 33-42 heavy atoms, but ring connectivity is often much less plausible than their component fragments. Typed/generic scaffolds are 476/352 versus Parent 450/347; the high cohort has only 19/7.
liabilities: O-O bonds occur in 170 of 870 Child outputs versus six Parent outputs; the seed-1 leader itself contains consecutive oxygen-oxygen bonds. This is a substantial chemical stability concern, even though this leader is not the highest one across seeds.

Eighty-three outputs contain a perceived ring of at most four atoms made entirely of aromatic atoms, including 45 of the high cohort. The cited contracted aromatic analogue flags geometrically problematic bonding; a sanitizable SMILES is not evidence of feasible aromatic geometry.
Thirty-one outputs are below six heavy atoms and 122 exceed fifty. Chloromethyl substituents and highly bridged acetals add reactivity and route complexity to the leaders.
missing_features: Less strained alternatives to the same connected aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are not demonstrated in the strongest dense-ring family. Their usefulness must be learned from feedback, not assumed from the score plateau.
A chemically conventional replacement for the O-O-O segment is missing from the cited seed-1 leader; the trajectory does not establish a benefit for peroxide chemistry.
Stereochemically defined bridged structures are absent: 314 outputs have potential tetrahedral centers and none is assigned.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The three Child seed leaders score 0.615454076367389, 0.6008878127522195 and 0.6271061188294413; Parent leaders were 0.6105466720544941, 0.6366578065410841 and 0.6314459049544995. Small disconnected-from-framework chemistry such as ClCCl, C and BrBr receives the observed 0.5 floor. The strongest seed-2 series retains an anilino linker and two core carbonyls. Its secondary anilino analogue scores 0.6268511416602749, while the cited N-methyl analogue scores 0.6127056115887091. Several peripheral substitutions share 0.6268511416602749. All 87 high-cohort graphs carry a carbonyl, and none exceeds fifty heavy atoms, despite 122 such oversized graphs in the full output. These data favor a particular connected architecture and linker arrangement locally; they do not show that additional fusion or halogenation is generally beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: Predominantly aromatic/partly saturated amine-containing molecules, median 32 heavy atoms and four rings, with twelve aromatic atoms and extensive halogen substitution. The high cohort is smaller at 24-32 heavy atoms, median 27. Seed 0 gives phenethylamine and aminomethyl substituents around an aryl-tetralin-like framework with thioether and fluorine; seed 1 gives cyclic tertiary/primary amine combinations with a thiol and a small unsaturated nitrogen ring; seed 2 gives larger aryl sulfinamide and partially unsaturated cyclic amine structures. The seed-0 leader looks more like a plausible medicinal-chemistry starting point than the strained leaders elsewhere, though stereochemistry and practical synthesis remain unresolved. Typed/generic scaffold counts are 363/231 versus Parent 355/234.
liabilities: Potential tetrahedral centers occur in 825 of 870 outputs, with no assigned configuration and no formal charges. Interpretation of a unique binding geometry is therefore limited.
Other families introduce thiols, hydroxylamine/N-O variants, small unsaturated rings and sulfinamides; their stability, sulfur stereochemistry and routes are not established by scoring.
Thirty-two accepted molecules have fewer than six heavy atoms and seven exceed fifty; these extremes include weak observations.
missing_features: A lack of amines is not the gap: the strongest structures already carry them. Missing is defined stereochemical presentation of those amines and aromatic groups; every high-cohort molecule has a potential tetrahedral center but none has assigned configuration.
Alternative complete amine/aromatic arrangements are less evident than variants of the seed-local families; the trajectory does not identify a universally preferred ring or linker.
The neutral SMILES do not document protonation-state coverage or justify a particular charged form.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The highest cited molecule scores 0.9942206504208195 and combines two aromatic rings with primary amine-bearing side chains and a saturated ring. All 87 high-cohort outputs match the audit non-amide neutral-amine pattern, compared with 24 of 87 low-cohort outputs. This is a connectivity descriptor, not a measured pKa. Low examples include a sulfonyl chloride at 0.0004426865581623269 and a halogenated anisole at 0.0012496378809616982; aromatic/halogen content alone does not reproduce the strong scores. Seed leaders are 0.9942206504208195, 0.9785347864466378 and 0.8756914141404031 versus Parent 0.9794504645558658, 0.9944816576523664 and 0.9970518791461749. The observed gradient supports an aromatic-plus-amine spatial arrangement, while the exact favorable geometry and ionization state remain unknown.

per_task.generated_character: Carbonyl- and nitrogen-rich polycycles dominate: median 32 heavy atoms, five rings and fifteen aromatic atoms across a 1-71 heavy-atom range. The seed-0 leader links a propyl aza-aromatic carbonyl unit to a cyclic diamine/lactam assembly. Seed 1 gives quinazoline-like fused aza-aromatics attached to bicyclic dicarbonyl nitrogen rings. Seed 2 retains a quinoline ether with densely connected N-N-containing cyclic structures. These have recognizable amine/amide fragments but can be synthetic targets of considerable complexity. Nonempty typed/generic scaffolds are 580/404 versus Parent 607/434; this is broad output chemistry, not a single collapsed scaffold.
liabilities: N-N bonds occur in 154 outputs and N-O bonds in 143; these counts cover multiple chemical environments and do not make every such bond intrinsically unsuitable, but several cited late structures are heavily entangled polycycles.
Thirty-four accepted outputs have fewer than six heavy atoms and nineteen exceed fifty.
The strongest graphs are less burdened by tiny fully aromatic perceived rings than the Parent high cohort, zero versus 63, but substantial stereochemical and route ambiguity remains.
missing_features: Broad scaffold variation is present; what remains unestablished is access to simpler, well-defined architectures preserving the observed aza-aromatic/carbonyl arrangement without repeatedly making dense fused or bridged nitrogen rings.
Assigned configurations are missing in 693 outputs with potential tetrahedral centers, including 85 of the 87 high-cohort molecules.
The score evidence does not specify a missing pharmacophore or establish that further ring growth would help.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited seed leaders score 0.22888797670990266, 0.22375027341296108 and 0.21332609167744657; Parent leaders were 0.21592303267069837, 0.2064837401424801 and 0.2266386345140889. The high cohort has median 27 heavy atoms, five rings, ten aromatic atoms and carbonyls in all 87 molecules. The low cohort has median thirteen heavy atoms, with C, C#C, O and FF at zero. An additional ring nitrogen in the seed-1 aromatic core accompanies 0.22375027341296108 versus 0.22302360319376838 for the cited close analogue, a small local difference. A substantial connected aza-aromatic/carbonyl architecture is associated with stronger observations, but similar scores across varied cyclic linkers provide little support for one missing exact scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The main family consists of compact nitrogen-rich carbonyl heterocycles carrying fluorinated small rings, amine/imine groups and variable aromatic or polyene substituents. Median size is 27 heavy atoms, five rings and six aromatic atoms; high-cohort sizes are 25-29 heavy atoms. Seed 0 contains a cyclic amidine/lactam-like core with fluoromethyl groups and a fluorocyclopropene. Seed 1 contains an N-fluorinated fused dicarbonyl core attached to a fluorinated cyclopropane and an amino-substituted ring or conjugated chain. Seed 2 reaches densely bridged, largely nonaromatic carbocycles attached to a dicarbonyl nitrogen core and gem-difluoro thiol-bearing cyclopropene. Graph coverage broadens to 365/208 typed/generic scaffolds versus Parent 200/105, but these are often chemically demanding structures.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds remain in 183 outputs, including 53 of the high cohort, despite falling from 472 in the Parent. The highest molecule contains two N-F bonds.

Small-ring motifs are present in 708 outputs. This does not condemn ordinary cyclopropanes, but the cyclopropenes, crowded bridged rings and 232 graphs with tiny fully aromatic perceived rings warrant geometric and synthetic scrutiny.
There are 45 outputs below six heavy atoms and five above fifty. Conjugated amino-polyenes and reactive thiol/N-F substitutions add stability uncertainty without assigned configurations.
missing_features: Conventional stable alternatives preserving the compact carbonyl/nitrogen/fluorine arrangement are not established in the strongest family; several top observations instead retain N-F bonds and strained small unsaturated rings.
Stereochemical identity is missing: 581 outputs have potential tetrahedral centers and none is assigned.

The trajectories do show carbon-bound fluorine and multiply halogenated carbon; lack of fluorination is not the gap. No exact missing functional group can be inferred as an objective requirement from these examples alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed leaders score 0.5644425722228507, 0.6565392184935046 and 0.37829072163839966, versus Parent 0.7327195754462501, 0.6174769250330556 and 0.5025353058534101. The strongest seed-1 product is the cited conjugated-chain analogue at 0.6565392184935046; the amino-substituted cyclic counterpart scores 0.5869409757886522. Within another close pair, N-F gives 0.5602802744487267 and N-methyl gives 0.5312585087353112. These are local associations, not evidence of chemical stability or universal N-fluorination benefit. All high-cohort molecules carry carbonyls and fit a compact size range, while the large repeated heterocyclic example scores 1.2904215118987727e-57 and a fluorine-only output scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. Both loss of architecture and excessive duplication can accompany extremely low scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-de8f05115faf, complete frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, accepted optimizer outputs only: N-halogen bonds occur in 326 of 4,350 molecules, O-halogen bonds in 126 and O-O bonds in 237. The paired Parent has 1,017, 104 and 48 respectively. A cited seed leader carries an O-O-O ring segment, and another highest-scoring example retains two N-F bonds. These are mixed changes in liabilities, not a uniform improvement or deterioration in chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically conventional fragment connectivity is not reliably retained while otherwise recognizable ring and carbonyl frameworks are elaborated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs the capability to vary size, polar groups and attachment positions while offering conventional bond environments alongside the unusual ones its present output explores. Stability and synthetic accessibility cannot be inferred from oracle scores. This evidence motivates a capability gap, not a prescribed exclusion filter or a claim that any one operator caused it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-de8f05115faf under the same frozen Search/evaluated-output scope: 177 of 4,350 outputs have fewer than six heavy atoms and 153 have more than fifty, versus 134 and 245 in n-7d1e6230ecce. C, F, BrBr and small oxygen/sulfur species occur among weak observations, while a much larger repeated heterocyclic example has score 1.2904215118987727e-57. None of the five highest-score cohorts contains either size tail.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently retain a complete molecular architecture when changing scaffold size.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic structural moves need the ability to preserve connected functional arrangements while altering size and scaffold identity in both directions. The observed association does not establish a universal size threshold or justify spending budget on an assumed target structure; usefulness must remain determined by actual current-session feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-de8f05115faf, all 4,350 accepted optimizer records on Search seeds 0/1/2: RDKit finds potential tetrahedral centers in 2,705 molecules and assigned centers in none. Parent n-7d1e6230ecce has 2,113 such molecules and likewise none assigned. The digest independently gives zero stereocentre-text rate for every covered output family. This includes rigid bridged structures and amine-bearing ring systems among the cited high-score molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic output is emitted without explicit tetrahedral configuration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A chemically explicit generator needs the capacity to introduce, preserve and compare valid stereochemical identities during structural changes. These records establish missing representation coverage, not that stereochemical enumeration improves the hidden score or that any specified configuration should be favored.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-de8f05115faf under the frozen Search/evaluated-output scope: 328 molecules contain an RDKit-perceived ring of at most four atoms whose atoms are all aromatic, versus 336 in the Parent. This flag is highly uneven across output families; one high-score cohort contains 45 such graphs out of 87, compared with zero in its Parent cohort. Other cited structures contain heavily bridged acetals or unsaturated small rings. The ring flag is a graph diagnostic, not a computed strain energy or proof that every small ring is impossible.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad ring generation is present, but geometrically credible ring connectivity is not reliably demonstrated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs access to ring replacement and reconnection that preserves feasible attachment geometry and chemically interpretable scaffolds. Ordinary small saturated rings remain legitimate chemistry; these observations do not prescribe banning them or identify the contribution of a particular ring-building component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-de8f05115faf, complete frozen Search panel: 2,038 nonempty typed Murcko scaffolds and 1,300 generic scaffolds occur across accepted outputs, versus Parent 1,880/1,234. Within the five high-score cohorts, generic scaffold counts are only 12, 7, 21, 25 and 15; peripheral analogues sometimes share exactly the same recorded score. Conventional carbonyl, aromatic and amine motifs coexist with increasing ring entanglement or reactive substitutions. These associations neither establish useful diversity nor isolate the effect of donor access.
transferable_gaps.gap: Rich graph novelty does not yet demonstrate reliable coverage of alternative complete frameworks with interpretable functional-group arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing capability is to reach alternative coherent frameworks while preserving useful local functional arrangements, rather than equating scaffold counts with chemical progress. Whether a new generator capability supplies useful alternatives must be tested with actual accepted feedback under its original Search conditions; no specific next intervention or component attribution follows from this report.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
